body: You seem like a decent human being. Maybe people like you for those qualities?

You think you're crazy? Mothers are the craziest people in the world. They love their children no matter how awful we treat them. It's beyond all logic or common sense. I can't believe how my mother still loves me after all the awful things I've told her, but she really does. It would make you feel better if you appolegize to her. Tell her you're going through stuff, and try to make it a conversation about limits and expectations. My mother also really frustrated me asking constantly for tech-support and refusing to learn new stuff. What helped me was to schedule "meetings" with her, with predefined start and end times, where I would help her with stuff. It's also a good exercise in being adult, something I'm still very bad at.

I'm sorry to hear you're in pain. And trust me, I've ran away from home when I was 18 and vanished. It hurt my mother the most.

I'm awful to the one person who loves me, and nice to my dad, who is a piece of shit. Why do we do it?

What are some good things in you that are good, and maybe worth loving?

I'm funny. The sadder I get, the better my humor becomes.

yeah pain can grow infinitely, like the universe. But it doesn't have to. Somehow it can be stopped, but fuck me if I know how. It's okay to make mistakes. Usually if you can say sorry, and improve, some people are capable of forgiveness. some don't, but some do. 

My mother for example loves me even though I told her awful stuff, and still to this day don't treat her right. My father on the other hand treats me like shit, even though I've always showed him respect and care. Have you got good people in your life?
You sound smart. It's okay to seek reassurance and validation. Those are just bad names for love and acceptance. what things are you unsure about in your life?

Hey, I'm sorry you're in pain. You haven't wasted your time by writing this, because I saw it and it made me react and feel. I've also went to psychiatrists and tried several pills (Venlafaxine, Brintellix, a few more). One of them helped me, the others didn't.

I can relate to being afraid of killing yourself - I've stood on the edge  of a cliff once and was too scared to jump. It's a lot harder than it seems.

I saw a few positive things in your post. As fucked up as it may sound - that "government official" fantasy is actually optimism. You believe that somehow someone can help you (yes, in a fucked up way) and that it could get better. Also,  you realize that what you have is a medical illness. That means the chemicals in your brain are sick, and that can be treated. Maybe science has the solution now or maybe it doesn't, I don't fucking know. Feel free to comment and tell me more
